chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Salih ibn Uqba from Bashir al-Dahhan who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Sometimes I miss the Hajj, so I go to recognize [the grave] at the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him).' He said, 'Well done, O Bashir! Whoever of the believers comes to the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), recognizing his right, on a day other than the day of Eid, Allah will write for him twenty Hajjs and twenty Umrahs, properly performed and accepted; and twenty Hajjs and Umrahs with a sent Prophet or a just Imam. And whoever comes to him on the day of Eid, Allah will write for him one hundred Hajjs and one hundred Umrahs and one hundred military expeditions with a sent Prophet or a just Imam.'

I said to him, 'How is it for me with the likes of the Standing (at Arafat)?' He looked at me as if slightly angry, then said to me, 'O Bashir! Indeed, when the believer comes to the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on the Day of Arafah, and performs Ghusl from the Euphrates, then turns his face towards him, Allah will write for him, with every step, a Hajj with its rituals — and I do not know except that he said: 'And a military expedition.'

key_terms.الْمَوْقِفُ: The Standing (referring to the ritual standing at Arafat during Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for visiting the grave of Imam Al-Husayn on the Day of Arafah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the theological elevation of Karbala as a spiritual axis, where the grave of Imam Al-Husayn (as) serves as a substitute for major acts of worship. The distinction between regular visits and the 'Day of Eid' (often interpreted as the anniversary of his martyrdom or a specific festive occasion) underscores the concept of *I'tiraf bi-hiqqihi* (acknowledging his right/status), linking physical pilgrimage to spiritual recognition. The specific mention of the Euphrates (*Al-Furat*) for Ghusl on the Day of Arafah connects the ritual purity of the Imam's resting place to the cosmic significance of the Prophet's pilgrimage, reinforcing the Shia view of the Ahl al-Bayt's central role in salvation history.
